Learning how to build world class financial models completely changed my career. It's allowed me to connect with impressive stakeholders, make a ton of money, and have a lot of fun along the way. In this video, I'm walking you through the exact template I've used across 100+ financial models as a fractional CFO.

Whether you're new to financial modeling or want to sharpen your skills, this complete walkthrough covers everything: the drivers tab concept, three statement models, error checking systems, revenue builds, headcount planning, and beautiful dashboards for stakeholders.

Inside this video, you'll discover:

- The "drivers tab" technique my manager's manager taught her that lets you control every assumption in your financial model from ONE centralized location (this single concept separates amateur models from professional ones)
- Why 99% of financial modelers are sitting on a ticking time bomb in their spreadsheets... and the simple error check system that catches mistakes BEFORE they reach the wrong person's inbox
- The $3 million headcount mistake I made early in my career... and the exact prorating formula that prevents you from ever understating cash burn like I did
- How to pull historical data using a "PBC format" and a single SUMIFS formula that works across hundreds of thousands of cells (no more manual data entry nightmares)
- WARNING: If you're not using color coded conventions in your models, investors and management will struggle to audit your work. Here's the exact color system professionals use (blue, black, purple, red) and when to use each
- The truth about revenue forecasting: there's no one size fits all template... but here's exactly how to structure builds for existing customers, pipeline deals, and new business so you can spot check where you were on and off
- Why your model should NEVER show sharp curves between actuals and projections (even if you have big plans for the future)... and how to review the "transition zone" that makes or breaks credibility with stakeholders
- How to transform raw financial data into a KPI dashboard that compares this month vs prior month vs prior year vs budget... all with a single button click

snippet.title: How Codex Automated One of the most hated Business Tasks
snippet.description:
One of the most repetitive yet complex (for AI) business tasks that AI previously couldn't do can now be done using Codex. Here's how:

Last three years working with non-tech traditional businesses, hundreds if not thousands of monthly people hours have gone to logging in and working in legacy software...many with user interfaces that pre-date 2010.

Things like Bid2Win, Vista, inEight, Caseware, ERP21 and so on. If you've ever used these systems you know the pain.

Most of these tools do not have an API that is easily accessible and forget MCPs or CLIs.

We have one client whose use case is one of the hardest to work through because there is a filter that loads quite long that leads to timeouts many AI tools.

This has been my mini Holy Grail the last year and and this was one of the very first things the client asked for two years ago

We tried everything from agent mode to Claude in Chrome to browser dev to playwright and so much more. 

It just couldn't complete this task and timeout or would take hours to do it and complete, especially the downloading the excel.

So the manual process is:
- Log into the software
- Two clicks to get to the filter page which takes a while to load
- Filter on specific reports to download via job number and tracking ID
- Download that report, an Excel file, into a folder 
- Then add a formula to that report that the team then could edit

The manual process took 9 minutes just to download the report because of the long load times. 

The Chrome Codex plug-in took 11 minutes and that included working on the Excel. Not to mention I could deploy multiple subagents to different tabs to do multiple extractions at once. 

Now we're in the process of deploying this capability to many of our clients who use legacy software that's pure web app-based. And for those legacy software that are desktop apps, we're testing computer use with them as well.

The Chrome Plugin for Codex is such a game changer for businesses working with legacy software. As you saw with this on, the load times were very slow and that was just for one report. Imagine running that for hundreds each month.

We know so many businesses doing this type of task that if Codex can do multiple of these in the background, this frees up their team significantly to complete most important tasks.

Have you tried the Chrome Plugin for Codex? What have you used it for?

snippet.title: Your AI Costs Are Rising: Token Costs Overtake Subscriptions
snippet.description:
In this video, you'll learn why to stop viewing AI business costs as simple subscription fees and why token allocation and agent workflows are changing corporate budgets. Many organizations are miscalculating their spending because they treat AI like traditional SaaS software. 


We look at how AI agent workflows consume resources at a different rate than standard chat interfacesWe also break down the financial reality behind modern AI adoption, specifically focusing on the shift from flat-rate subscriptions to consumption-based pricing models. By understanding token allocation, you can better forecast your actual spend versus your estimated budget.
